drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. Subject to client approval and agreement on a complete document, Vireo proposes a $350,000 annual base salary and twelve months of salary continuation, with continued employer contributions toward health coverage, for termination without Cause or resignation for Good Reason. We have included defined triggers and notice and cure protections. We can agree to delete the post-employment non-compete and propose confidentiality and a narrowly limited employee non-solicitation covenant instead, subject to applicable law. The attached revisions remain subject to completion of the agreement and review of the applicable jurisdiction’s requirements.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $350,000 (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to required withholding. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans generally available to similarly situated executives, subject to their terms.

3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, other than due to death or disability, or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay twelve months of the Executive’s then-current Base Salary in regular payroll installments and, if the Executive timely elects continuation health coverage, continue its employer contribution toward that coverage for up to twelve months, ending earlier upon eligibility for comparable coverage with a new employer. Severance is conditioned on execution and non-revocation of a customary release of employment-related claims within sixty days after termination; the release shall not waive rights to accrued compensation, vested benefits, indemnification, or enforcement of this Agreement. Salary continuation shall commence on the first regular payroll date after that sixty-day period, with a catch-up payment for intervening installments, subject to applicable tax requirements. Accrued salary, reimbursable expenses, and vested benefits shall be paid regardless of execution of a release. “Cause” means fraud, embezzlement, or material misappropriation involving the Company; conviction of, or a guilty or no-contest plea to, a felony involving dishonesty; willful misconduct causing material harm to the Company; or a material breach of this Agreement or willful, continued failure to perform lawful material duties. Cause requires written notice specifying the grounds and a reasonable opportunity to respond, and, for any curable grounds, thirty days to cure. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in Base Salary, a material diminution in authority or responsibilities, relocation of the principal work location by more than fifty miles, or a material breach of this Agreement by the Company. The Executive must give written notice within sixty days after learning of the condition, allow thirty days for cure, and resign within thirty days after the cure period expires if the condition remains uncured.

4. CONFIDENTIALITY AND LIMITED NON-SOLICITATION. No post-employment non-compete shall apply. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential business information except in performing duties for the Company or as authorized or required by law. Confidential information excludes information publicly available other than through a breach, lawfully obtained from another source without a confidentiality obligation, or independently developed without use of Company confidential information. Nothing prohibits protected whistleblowing, reporting possible legal violations to government authorities, cooperating with investigations, discussing matters protected by applicable employment law, or other legally protected disclosures; no prior authorization or notice to the Company is required for such activity. For six months after employment ends, and only to the extent permitted by applicable law, the Executive shall not directly and specifically solicit for employment any Company employee with whom the Executive worked materially during the preceding twelve months. General advertisements, unsolicited approaches, and hiring without prohibited solicitation are excluded.
